--- CHUNK 1 ---
Colombo. To the Esteemed Gentlemen Anthony Mooijaert and Marten Rein, Commanders of the commandments of Jaffanapatnam and Candy, as well as the Members of the Secret Committee, Esteemed Commanding Gentlemen of Trincomalee. By letter of the 29th of April, we were informed that the fugitive Kandyan prince was said to be hiding in a forest at Welletje on a mountain and was intending to dispatch envoys to the Coromandel Coast. We could not refrain from fulfilling our duty and have deemed it proper to inform your Esteemed Lordships, under the enclosure of the copy of the aforementioned letter hereto attached, of the required knowledge. With the addition that upon receipt of that letter, we have repeatedly ordered the subordinate posts to maintain a watchful eye both on arriving and departing persons, and thereby also to prevent or intercept all correspondence. With which honor we have, undertaking to name ourselves, Esteemed Commanding Gentlemen, your Esteemed Lordships' obedient and obedient servants, was signed N. A. Lebek, H. Hogerwaerd, J. Herthum, M. van Hek, A. Wierman, J. Panneel, and C. F. Schreu, in the margin Jaffanapatnam the 1st of May, Anno 1765. To the aforementioned. The time having arrived, with the passing of the southwest monsoon, to have the cruising boats stationed at Punto Pedro to Trincomalee along the Wanliasse

--- CHUNK 2 ---
With which honor we have, undertaking to name ourselves, Esteemed Commanding Gentlemen, your Esteemed Lordships' obedient and obedient servants, was signed N. A. Lebek, H. Hogerwaerd, J. Herthum, M. van Hek, A. Wierman, J. Panneel, and C. F. Schreu, in the margin Jaffanapatnam the 1st of May, Anno 1765. To the aforementioned. The time having arrived, with the passing of the southwest monsoon, to have the cruising boats stationed at Punto Pedro to Trincomalee along the Wanliasse shores to be stationed, so as on that side to prevent all smuggling as well as to maintain a watchful eye on the movements of the Kandyan Court regarding what the Trincomalee servants reported in their secret letter of the 19th of April, recently past, of which by these our separate letters of the 1st of May the Esteemed Gentlemen have had your Esteemed Lordships' copy made known. Supposing thus, we take the liberty, Esteemed Gentlemen, to request the qualification of freedom for your Esteemed Lordships to employ two of the cruising Pattamars around Manaar, five in number, as we then further undertake regarding our above-mentioned garrison and of manpower-depleted posts Aripo and elsewhere to submit to your Esteemed Lordships for decision whether the command thus long lying at Palemanaer should be maintained to prevent that from the Rameswaram Court in service of the Kandyan prince, no such men as mentioned in the Kilkari letter of the 13th of March, of which the Manaar servants have sent your Esteemed Lordships a copy, should make any landing thereabouts. Now since in this monsoon at that place a boat lying aground and as it were on that side a landing is impossible to be made, it could not be withdrawn, the more so since the heavy costs of the greater supply to the detached forces will cease and the manpower and garrisons, which are closely by the works, will be freed from

--- CHUNK 3 ---
of the Manaar servants have sent your Esteemed Lordships a copy, should make any landing thereabouts. Now since in this monsoon at that place a boat lying aground and as it were on that side a landing is impossible to be made, it could not be withdrawn, the more so since the heavy costs of the greater supply to the detached forces will cease and the manpower and garrisons, which are closely by the works, will be freed from the discomforts and the feared sicknesses which, when the rainy season might surprise them on that flat meadow where they are stationed, will certainly befall them. We do so in hope of good tidings, that proposal to you, insofar as no further news from Kilkari regarding what was then rumored there and come to the ears of the resident Keunneman, having received the rumor, we suppose that the same will have since disappeared again. And on account of the weak garrison both here and at Manaar, we are thereby compelled, but we leave the decision to the wiser judgment of your Esteemed Lordships, who will be informed from nearby, deferred to furnish us in that regard with their esteemed order. Meanwhile, for the rest, we have the honor to name ourselves with all high regard, undertaking as aforementioned, signed A. Lebeck, H. Hogerwaerd, J. Herthum, M. van Hek, A. Wierman, I. Panneel, and O. F. Schreuder, in the margin Jaffanapatnam the 4th of June, Anno 1765. To the aforementioned. We having been honored to approve, upon receipt of your Esteemed Lordships' separate letter dated the 8th of this month, that upon the arrival of the Sipahis marching according to the content of that letter, we shall first have one company of equal soldiers stationed here sent forth with the officers belonging thereto. Meanwhile, we have the honor to

--- CHUNK 4 ---
in the margin Jaffanapatnam the 4th of June, Anno 1765. To the aforementioned. We having been honored to approve, upon receipt of your Esteemed Lordships' separate letter dated the 8th of this month, that upon the arrival of the Sipahis marching according to the content of that letter, we shall first have one company of equal soldiers stationed here sent forth with the officers belonging thereto. Meanwhile, we have the honor to name ourselves with all high regard, undertaking as aforementioned, signed A. Lebeck, in the margin Jaffanapatnam the 23rd of July, Anno 1765. To the aforementioned. By secret resolution of the 2nd of this month, having resolved to employ two of the cruising Pattamars around Manaar, five in number, for the usual yearly cruising east of Punto Pedro to Trincomalee along the Wanliasse shores, on the one hand since the southwest monsoon has long been in progress and thus the best time is to watch for the smugglers who from the bay and the opposite shore gladly take their course on that side, and on the other side to maintain a watchful eye on the movements of the Jaffna Court, which the Trincomalee servants reported in their secret letter of the 19th of April, recently past, of which by our separate letters of the 1st of May your Esteemed Lordships have received a copy, and of which also our submission of the 4th of June makes mention, the supposed movement of the Kandyan court. Thus we have to your Esteemed Lordships the most dutiful report to make in hope that this closes our Colombo matter as well as that since the aforementioned two Pattamars have been called upon for the general purpose, the esteemed approval of the highest authority will come to bear, the more so since this cruising, as said, yearly, even with the beginning of this monsoon or whenever the same has afforded any opportunity therefor, has taken place.

--- CHUNK 5 ---

Thus we have to your Esteemed Lordships the most dutiful report to make in hope that this closes our Colombo matter as well as that since the aforementioned two Pattamars have been called upon for the general purpose, the esteemed approval of the highest authority will come to bear, the more so since this cruising, as said, yearly, even with the beginning of this monsoon or whenever the same has afforded any opportunity therefor, has taken place. Meanwhile, for the rest, we have the honor to name ourselves with all high regard, undertaking as aforementioned, signed A. Lebeck, H. Hogerwaard, I. Herthum, M. van Hek, L. v. d. Spar, I. Wierman, I. Panneel, and E. F. Schreuder, in the margin Jaffanapatnam the 7th of August, Anno 1765. To the well-esteemed, greatly esteemed gentleman, Mr. Jman Willem Falck, Governor and Director of the Island of Ceylon and its dependencies. Well-esteemed, greatly esteemed, high commanding gentleman. Upon receipt of your well-esteemed, greatly esteemed, honored letter of the 2nd of this month written to the Manaar chief Schorer and hereby sent to me in copy under covering letters of the 15th, together with the enclosures cited therein, first, for the execution of the aforementioned eye-work of the Kandyans under this jurisdiction, all necessary orders have been placed, and the Pattamars, the beacon, and the peace which had returned from the cruising post between Punto Pedro and Trincomalee according to requisition have likewise been projected for the cruising of the places indicated by your well-esteemed, greatly esteemed letter, and for that purpose the aforementioned Manaar chief has been assigned and ordered the arrangement, and by which meanwhile the Pattamars, the Constancy, and the supervision together with a cruising thonij, the first to cruise at Pezale and the last at Jallemanaar, have already been employed, of which I find myself obliged to your well-esteemed, greatly esteemed lordship to report with further respect.

--- CHUNK 1 ---
the bidding has returned, and has likewise been projected for the cruising of the places indicated by your Esteemed Excellency in the aforementioned missive, and for that purpose the aforementioned Manaar chief has been assigned and ordered the arrangement, by which in the meantime the patchallans [local vessels], the Constancy and vigilance, together with a cruising thonij [small vessel] the first at Pezale and the last at Jallemanaer, have already been employed, of which I find myself obliged to report to your Esteemed Excellency with further respect, noting that along the standing posts already by Billet on severe and according to the exigency of matters, life and death penalty, adhering to the orders existing on that point, we have forbidden anyone to transport across the water with their thonijs or vessels, and also that from our Garrison some European and sipahi [Indian soldier] troops for the strengthening of the inland warriors have been detached to the shore around Jlle Pecauwe, in order not only to guard the same and to prevent the landing at the side of the wanni entirely, but also thereabouts to cut off the passage for the Kandyan missionaries and further to be at the works, should they be required on that side or elsewhere. In respectful confidence that these adopted measures will receive the esteemed approval of your Esteemed Excellency, I have the honor with all due high regard to be /:signed:/ your Esteemed Excellency, High Commanding Lord, your Esteemed Excellency's obedient and obedient Servant was signed A: Mooijaert in margin Jaffanapatnam the 19th of October, Year 1765. Agrees J. dan Hemtous

--- CHUNK 2 ---
was signed A: Mooijaert in margin Jaffanapatnam the 19th of October, Year 1765. Agrees J. dan Hemtous

--- CHUNK 3 ---
Outgoing Letters to Jaffanapatnam
To the Chief Merchant and Dessave [administrator] D. E. Noel Anthonij Lebeck: as Pro-interim commanding officer there. Esteemed, Discreet and Particular Good Friend. You have today had two companies of sipahis march overland from here to there, as mentioned in the enclosed brief strength, whereby is also noted what they have received in wages, etc., and the Manaar servants have been ordered to maintain one company thereof and in its place to send the company of sipahis described with him back here with all speed, and the other to continue marching forward to your location. Upon arrival of the same, you must hold them there and in its place send back here with all haste the strongest company of sipahis from the Manaar, the worthy provided Discreet two at your command, together with the officers belonging thereto, with which after greeting remain /:signed:/ Esteemed, Discreet and Particular Good Friend, your Good Friend /:was signed:/ A. Mooijaart /:in margin:/ Colombo the 8th of July, Year 1765. 

Jaffanapatnam
To the Lord Commander Anthonij Mooijaart
From the Residents at Kilkare, having received word that two Kandyan missionaries disguised in Moorish clothing arrived at Naoer with an inland vessel, this serves as proof that there is poor vigilance; wherefore we insist most strongly on our order by missive of the 10th of this month to cruise diligently and keep a watchful eye on all suspicious foreigners, your Excellency being qualified for that purpose by publication and affixing of bills, promising a premium of 500 rixdollars [modern equivalent: approximately 500 Dutch guilders] to those who apprehend and report such Kandyan missionaries, such that they fall into our hands, with which after greeting remain /:signed:/ Mighty, worthy, Discreet, your Good Friend /:signed:/ Im: will: Falck /:in margin:/ Colombo the 23rd of September, Year 1765. 

To the same as before
Your Excellency is ordered to prevent most strictly the transport of salt to the upper lands

--- CHUNK 4 ---
hold most strictly to our order; your Excellency being qualified for that purpose by publication and affixing of bills, promising a premium of 500 rixdollars [modern equivalent: approximately 500 Dutch guilders] to those who apprehend and report such Kandyan missionaries, such that they fall into our hands, with which after greeting remain /:signed:/ Mighty, worthy, Discreet, your Good Friend /:signed:/ Im: will: Falck /:in margin:/ Colombo the 23rd of September, Year 1765. 

To the same as before
Your Excellency is ordered to prevent most strictly the transport of salt to the upper lands: for that purpose the Lascorin [local militia] posts at the Jagerboom and Wedeltivoe are to be doubled and strict orders are to be placed, that they must absolutely at the first-mentioned place allow no corl [unit of measurement for salt] salt to pass. To other places also no more salt must be transported than for the necessity of the community, from which are expressly excluded the hostile wannias [local rulers] and natural Kandyans. Also the post holder of Arripo must for that purpose have the Laskorins patrol strongly, and if necessary be assisted with sipahis from Manaar: cited letter to Manaar. Furthermore, we expect from your Excellency a statement of the wages, etc., received by the sipahis who have been with you since the day of their arrival there, with which after greeting remain /:signed:/ as before /:signed:/ I: w: Falck /:in margin:/ Colombo the 26th of September, 1765. 

To the same as before
From the enclosed copy of the missive to the Manaar servants, you will understand our intention regarding the enclosing and cruising of the sea harbors, which is in the matter of the Kattaseuver and the apprehension and arrest of its vessels, and you will see the good and /:dated:/ 24th September. We let this serve to order you to contribute everything in your power to the advancement of this our objective, and for that purpose to send 1 or 2 armed vessels, such as you best have at hand

--- CHUNK 5 ---
intention regarding the enclosing and cruising of the sea harbors, which is in the matter of the Kattaseuver and the apprehension and arrest of its vessels, and you will see the good and /:dated:/ 24th September. We let this serve to order you to contribute everything in your power to the advancement of this our objective, and for that purpose to send 1 or 2 armed vessels, such as you best have at hand to the Bay of Tondij, with such orders as are prescribed in the enclosures for the cruisers of Manaar, with which after friendly greeting remain /:signed:/ as before. By order, etc.: /:signed:/ Ioan Gerrard van Angelbeek, Secretary /:in margin:/ Colombo the 25th of September, Year 1765. 

Jaffanapatnam and Manaar
To the Lord Commander Anthonij Mooijaart
And the Chief, the Under-Merchant Ian Willem Schorer
Together with the Council
Mighty, worthy, Discreet, Good Friends. Upon receipt of further news of the overfall, we have deemed it good to rescind our order given to you by letters of the 24th of this month with respect to the Teuversen; accordingly the same must remain outside execution, but having already been executed, we order hereby to release the persons and goods that may have been arrested by virtue thereof at the earliest, to recall the cruisers, should they have already departed. With which after greeting remain /:signed:/ as before /:signed:/ Im: will: Falck, I: I: Feber, I: n: J: van Angelbeek, A Moens and I: H: Borwater /:in margin:/ Colombo the 28th of September, 1765. /:below:/ P.S. The Kilkare Resident's customs officer has sent via Manaar to the first signed a letter dated the 23rd of this month, on whose speedy and safe delivery much depends: for which purpose your Excellency is hereby recommended, should that letter upon receipt of this

--- CHUNK 1 ---
after greetings remain [as before] signed: Im: will: Falek I: I: Feber I:n J: van Angelbeek, A Moens and I: H: Borwater [in margin:] Colombo the 28th of September 1765. [below:] P: S: the kilkareese Resident keunemans has sent over to Manaar to the first signatory a letter dated the 23rd of this month, to whose speedy and safe delivery to Saffrena much depends: for which purpose you are hereby recommended, if that letter had not already been sent from here upon receipt of this. To the Departing and Arriving Commanders Anthonij Mooijaart and Noel Anthonij Lebeck, Stalwart, Prudent, Discreet. With the last of January the 2 companies of sipahis [Indian soldiers] who garrison Manaar and Jaffna must be discharged and provision made for their transport to Nagapatnam after they shall have been issued half a month's travel allowance. On the other hand, you may from the siparis [soldiers] whom the Lieutenant Cetanche has recruited and whose latest transport is to be expected with you at that time, retain one or two companies, if needed, although it appears to me that one company for Manaar is sufficient, since now the military of all Patjallangs can be relieved. I remain after greetings [as before] as before. By order &: [signed:] I: G: van Angelbeek secretary [in margin:] Colombo the 28th of December A.o 1765. Agrees Tommis temoous E: k: vant ph: Committee

--- CHUNK 2 ---
Colombo. To the Well Esteemed, Greatly Honored Sir. Lubbert Jan van Eck, Extraordinary Councillor of India, Governor and Director of the Island of Ceylon with its dependencies. Well Esteemed, Greatly Honored, High Commanding Sir, your well esteemed, greatly honored much valued order and directive contained in the letter of the 28th of March last concerning the preparation of the ship Schoonzigt so that it may be able to proceed to Malacca upon your further order, I shall not fail to observe with all possible speed and due secrecy. Meanwhile with all veneration I have the honor to remain [as before] well esteemed, greatly honored, your highly commanding sir, greatly esteemed, greatly honored, most obedient and faithfully devoted servant [was signed:] A: Samland [in margin:] Gale the 1st of April A.o 1765. Colombo. To the E: Sir Iassenas Commander Anthonij Mooijaert and the members thereof presently constituting the Secret Council there. E: Sir and Particularly Good Friends. Having informed myself regarding the number or quantity of coolies which could be brought together in the Districts of Gale and Mature to be available at the proper time, I now report to you, E: your inquiry in this regard, that Mature has thereupon given a stated quantity of three to four hundred heads, including all sorts of servants who can be pressed into coolie service, as well as those from the Gale district in the same manner more or less one hundred pieces of those peoples. But since nothing is directly known to me regarding the subjection of the Colom[bo] corle to the Company, much less of the circumstances thereof or what will undoubtedly further belong to such an important assignment, I must declare after repeated consideration that I am not in a position in a matter of such great importance to me to

--- CHUNK 3 ---
Gale district in the same manner more or less one hundred pieces of those peoples. But since nothing is directly known to me regarding the subjection of the Colom[bo] corle to the Company, much less of the circumstances thereof or what will undoubtedly further belong to such an important assignment, I must declare after repeated consideration that I am not in a position in a matter of such great importance to me to the one or the other placed in consideration by you, that is, whether to the appointment of heads over the aforementioned territories from the Company's own old inland servants, or to the continuation of those who have been declared to be subjected together with the aforesaid Colonna Corle, to advise regarding this or concerning the further requisites to deliberate upon the means and to provide guidance. For the rest, I have made known the written order regarding the discharge of certain inland warriors serving under the Modliaer Tillekeratne and further deemed unnecessary by your E:E: in the Matureesche Dessavonijs by Extract from your E:E: general directive to the E: Dessave, to the understanding of his E: that the said discharge has also taken place immediately thereupon. Herewith I have the honor after my kind greetings to remain [as before] E: Sir and Particular Good Friends, your E:E: willing friend [was signed:] A: Samlant [in margin:] Gale the 5th of June Anno 1765. To as before. Upon receipt of your E: E: letter of the 1st of this month I did not fail to immediately and with the most forceful recommendations to comply in the most complete manner with the requisite contained therein, both to the E: Dessave De Lij as well as to the overseer of the Gale-Korle Stroebe, to charge them with the speedy gathering and provision of coolies and beasts of burden for

[in margin:] Gale the 5th of June Anno 1765. To as before. Upon receipt of your E: E: letter of the 1st of this month I did not fail to immediately and with the most forceful recommendations to comply in the most complete manner with the requisite contained therein, both to the E: Dessave De Lij as well as to the overseer of the Gale-Korle Stroebe, to charge them with the speedy gathering and provision of coolies and beasts of burden for the service of the forthcoming Expedition to Kandy, as well as from both the one and the other both their serious promise and assurance obtained that they will neglect nothing to comply therewith with all available means here, and I shall also not fail to set them further to it with the utmost force. Herewith I have the honor after my kind greetings to remain [as before] A: Samlant as before [signed:] and [in margin:] Pale the 6th of July A.o [To as before.] I have upon receipt of your E:E: letter of the 20th of this month ordered all possible measures to obtain as many coolies as possible and with the utmost speed that can possibly be, the heads of those peoples being here and in the land, whereupon on the foregoing rumors of such seizures of servants at Costij and elsewhere nothing, parties of Moors had taken flight and Etc: daily do so upon the recommendations still made to them without serious distinction thereto with all available means, just as the E: Dessave in the Matureesche also promises to do all that is possible, although most of those who assisted in the previous campaign are sick on that side and for such a gathering of peoples far and wide their dwelling will require some time. Furthermore, the requested party of beasts of burden

--- CHUNK 5 ---
had taken flight and Etc: daily do so upon the recommendations still made to them without serious distinction thereto with all available means, just as the E: Dessave in the Matureesche also promises to do all that is possible, although most of those who assisted in the previous campaign are sick on that side and for such a gathering of peoples far and wide their dwelling will require some time. Furthermore, the requested party of beasts of burden from both the Matureesche as well as here has been amply provided and from the Singhalese servants also successively sent as many men as with the utmost effort have been able to be obtained thus far, as evidenced by the enclosed list, and with which also without delay we proceed further, and if it should be possible to be able to obtain further obligations beyond this, everything shall be contributed and nothing neglected, although for this, as said, time and delay above all is required, which upon your E: E: further inquiry, as one cannot commit oneself therein, in answer Colombo. herewith I shall after my kind greetings remain [as before] as before [signed:] A: Samlant [in margin:] Gale the 25th of July Anno 1765. To the Well Esteemed, Greatly Honored Sir, M: Iman Willem Falck, Governor and Director of the Island of Ceylon with its dependencies. Well Esteemed, Greatly Honored, Greatly Honored, High Commanding Sir! Having had the honor to receive your well esteemed, greatly honored, secret separate letters of the 19th of this month, I have thereupon in respect to the first as well to the Lieutenant Hansz: at Pittigelleand the post-holding Sergeant at Bentotte written and ordered the necessary measures for the proper execution of your well esteemed, greatly honored decision and order contained therein, not doubting that the one and the other shall be To as before.

--- CHUNK 1 ---
Commanding Sir! Having had the honor to receive your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed secret separate letters of the 19th of this month, I have thereupon, in respect, first of all written to and ordered both Lieutenant Hans at Pittigelle and the post-holding Sergeant at Bentotte the necessary instructions for the proper execution of your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed decision and order contained therein, not doubting that one and the other will be executed properly as before. Although the aforementioned officer Hans will need a few days' time to prepare himself for his departure and also to take with him from there and deliver to Bentotte the remaining provisions, gunpowder, lead, etc., which may be on hand there, meanwhile also the overseer of the Gale Corle will have a small Lascorin [uncertain: possibly a type of vessel or equipment] prepared in readiness to be sent there and placed under a European Corporal. I take the liberty of being with deep reverence your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed High Commanding Sir your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed obedient and obedient Servant, was signed A. Samlant in the margin Gale on the 22nd of August in the year 1765. — Three packages with goods for military equipment, moreover your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed very respected of the 26th of August, having been ordered to me by land, I have not failed to have the same unopened immediately delivered and given to the Commanding Captain Franken for his responsibility. I have had the honor by this respectful communication with the utmost respect most humbly to be able to be /undestood/ as before /Signed/ Asamlant and in the margin Gale on the 13th of September in the year 1765. I have had the honor to receive your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed venerated missive of the 6th of this month, upon which most humbly I report that orders have been immediately given for the preparation of all

--- CHUNK 2 ---
tain Franken for his responsibility and given to him. I have had the honor by this respectful communication with the utmost respect most humbly to be able to be /understood/ as before /Signed/ Asamlant and in the margin Gale on the 13th of September in the year 1765. I have had the honor to receive your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed venerated missive of the 6th of this month, upon which most humbly I report that orders have been immediately given for the preparation of all the necessary items for the storage and housing of the Coolies [Koelis: indigenous laborers/soldiers] inland militia to arrive at Bentotte according to your most esteemed good pleasure, in order to take post there. I have furthermore taken the liberty of being with the deepest respect most humbly your understood as before signed A. Samlant in the margin As before. Gale on the 8th of October in the year 1765. Your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed esteemed writing concerning the repatriating friends as well as the three non-commissioned officers of the militia who have also been licensed thereto, I shall not fail to observe properly. I take the liberty hereby to make respectful report that the ordered guard houses and lodgings at Bentotte, according to the report of the overseer Stroebbe, have been constructed and are ready for the storage of the inland military post that is expected there. Herewith I take the liberty of being with deep respectfulness able to be /understood as before signed A. Samlant /in the margin Gale on the 16th of September 1765. As before. I have had the honor to receive the very venerated letter of your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed containing the order to send the parties of Coolies required according to the attached list from the districts of this Commandment, and upon which most humbly I report that the orders for the procurement and fulfillment of that requisition have been immediately dispatched by me with all earnestness and emphasis to the Esteemed Dessave at Mature and the overseer of the

--- CHUNK 3 ---
as before. I have had the honor to receive the very venerated letter of your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed containing the order to send the parties of Coolies required according to the attached list from the districts of this Commandment, and upon which most humbly I report that the orders for the procurement and fulfillment of that requisition have been immediately dispatched by me with all earnestness and emphasis to the Esteemed Dessave at Mature and the overseer of the Gale Corle, and having been taken up by both for proper compliance as much as possible, I have in the meantime also received reports both from Mature and from the Gale district that good parties for this service are coming into readiness in order to march to Costigal [uncertain: place name] before long. I hope and wish most heartily that through a complete fulfillment of these required peoples your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed satisfaction may be brought about. And I take the liberty of being with all veneration most humbly /understood as before /signed/ A. Samlant in the margin Gale on the 17th of December in the year 1765. As before. I have the honor most humbly to answer your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed very venerated of the 21st of this month, that to the Esteemed Major Medelen the pleasure of your Highest has been announced to proceed there with the greatest speed, and by his Esteemed it has also been taken into observance. For the transport of the same there can still serve the 25 heads for the completion of the 480 serviceable still remaining requested by your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed from the Gale Corle, thus according to the received report of the overseer of the said Gale Corle, of which 455 heads have already passed Bentotte and continued their journey there. Furthermore I take the liberty to present to your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed the name roll of the eastern military under Captain Boeang Mangadoea, such as they

--- CHUNK 4 ---
themselves can still serve the 25 heads for the completion of the 480 serviceable still remaining requested by your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed from the Gale Corle, thus according to the received report of the overseer of the said Gale Corle, of which 455 heads have already passed Bentotte and continued their journey there. Furthermore I take the liberty to present to your Well Noble Strict Great Esteemed the name roll of the eastern military under Captain Boeang Mangadoea, such as they were dispatched from Tangale and arrived here yesterday in order, in accordance with your Highest order by letter sent here on the 9th of this month, to do garrison service here until further order, and herewith with deep reverence and respectfulness I take myself /understood as before signed A. Samlandt in the margin Gale on the 24th of December in the year 1765. _ Agrees Joannes Hamtout Esteemed member of the secret committee

--- CHUNK 5 ---
To the Mister Commandeur Abraham Samlant Stalwart, Provident, Discreet! The enclosed letter addressed to the Commissioner of the district Willem van Damast Limberger should first of all be delivered to the same, but since he has already departed, it should be sent back here. Wherewith after greeting remain /understood/ Stalwart, Provident, Discreet your Esteemed Good friend /was signed/ M. Rein /in the margin/ Colombo on the 30th of January in the year 1765. As before. The enclosed packet from the Secret Committee here addressed to Their High Lordships, if the ship Lekkerland has not yet departed from there, shall be given to its captain as such a packet should be, but in the contrary case, to be sent back, wherewith after greeting remain /understood/ as before /signed/ M. Rein /in the margin Colombo on the 31st of January in the year 1765. As before. Since in the months of July and August coming, all coolies that can possibly be gathered will be needed for the service of a general Expedition that is planned to be undertaken at that time, we have wished to inquire of you in good time as to the number of coolies that could be gathered in the District of Tale and the Cassaronije [Cassaronije: administrative division] of Mature for that purpose, in order that we may take our further measures accordingly. Since the operations in the said Dessavonie [Dessavonie: administrative division] and adjoining kingdoms' lands will presumably already have ceased, or otherwise must be stopped, and thus the keeping in service of the inland warriors under Sillekeratne Modliaer would only cause unnecessary costs, so please let your Esteemed the Dessave De Lij order them to be discharged at the earliest, or at the latest at the end of this month. That the Corle column has submitted itself to the Esteemed Company, the said Esteemed De Lij aforementioned will already have reported to your Esteemed. Esteemed and respectable gentlemen,

By means of the enclosed copy of a Kilkare letter dated the 12th of this month, your esteemed gentlemen will come to understand the movements which the followers of the king fled from the court of Kandy are newly beginning to make at the Rameswaram court. Thus I take the liberty to most dutifully communicate the same to you and at the same time to offer a missive received from the aforementioned Kilkare, for which and all other matters this being directed most humbly, I have the honor otherwise to sign this with much respect. Your esteemed gentlemen's commanding lords, your esteemed gentlemen's humble and obedient servant, signed I. W. Schorer. In the margin: Manner, the 17th of May, Anno 1765.

To the aforementioned, the Sipahis [Indian soldiers] consisting of two companies, mentioned in your esteemed gentlemen's respected letters of the 8th of this month, which came overland as well as 28 men who departed from there by inland vessel toward here, have arrived here. Standing ready for tomorrow, the aforementioned 28 men, since there are many sick and weak among them, are to be sent forward by vessel to Jaffnapatnam. To the most noble, greatly esteemed Lord Mr. Jman Willem Falck, Governor and Director of the Island of Ceylon and its dependencies.

Most noble, greatly esteemed, highly commanding Lord,

The Kilkare servants, as evidenced by their letter herewith most humbly enclosed and communicated to us, have reported that some Kandyans in Moorish dress arrived at Nacaur with an inland vessel and subsequently, with the help of the Tanjore prince as well as the Chancellor of the Treasury of the Theuver, sought to seize some war troops in order with the same to land at Pesale and Tallemanaer, as well as the bay of Mudenpattu, Illipe Carre, which is the western shore of the Wanni. Thus we are obliged to give your most noble, greatly esteemed Lord most respectful knowledge of this and most humbly to request that through your most noble, greatly esteemed care we may be assisted with a company of good Sipahis or Malays, since the Sipahis stationed here as well as at Jaffnapatnam are for the most part sick, weak, and impotent, and with the same no least resistance can be made in case of need.

To Jan Feber and Jan P. van Angelbeek [in margin:] Colombo, the 10th of July 1765:

Our European military force has suffered so greatly through the nearly continuous marching back and forth that we are compelled to have more than one hundred men from the Colombo garrison, who have become unfit for service partly through wounds, partly through weakness and chronic illnesses, sent back to Europe, besides those who have chosen to be sent to Batavia, or whom we must distribute here and there in places where the service is easier; and besides a considerable number who are unfit at the detachments in the field and in the remaining garrisons outside Colombo, through sickness and disease, and cannot be used for any command. Since, moreover, the four ships that have arrived have brought scarcely 500 healthy soldiers instead of the promised 800, we find ourselves greatly hindered in being able to fill the positions of the fallen, wounded, and unfit, at some very weakened companies, and we are therefore compelled to seek assistance from your Excellency. If we could only be supported with one hundred common soldiers from the Coromandel garrisons, we would see ourselves relieved from our predicament for the time being, and we bind ourselves to repay your Excellency's assistance with double the number at the slightest change of affairs for the better (which God grant). As before. As before. We also send your Excellency by Lieutenant Letanche a model cartridge pouch, which we request be made as soon as possible in the quantity needed and sent back here with the return of the aforementioned commandant, with which we remain with respectful greetings and esteem. [signed below:] as before [signed:] Im. will. Falck, Jan J. and Jan P. van Angelbeek [in margin:] Colombo, the 10th of July 1765:
